name: GraveyardWoolCaper
source:
His mother's funeral was terrible for Jake, but coming back the next day to find a piece of black wool tied around her gravestone sparked intrigue rather than anger. The piece of wool seemed to be still connected to something. He followed the piece of wool through the graveyard and ended up right at the door of a mausoleum. He tentatively walked inside, afraid to disturb the living, when he was suddenly attacked from behind. Luckily for him, his assailant was an odd, odd man and had tried to bash him head in with an old, rusted trumpet which did nothing but give him a little bit of tetanus. Jake recovered quickly, and punched the man in the face. 
 
 As the man stumbled outside the mausoleum and into the sunlight, Jake noticed that he had on a monocle and a top hat. More confused and more intrigued than he was earlier, he went out to confront the man. But before he could get a word out, the man hopped out of sight. Jake searched for the man, but could n't find him. He turned to go back into the mausoleum. Hearing something behind him, Jake turned around to see that the man was rushing at him on a pennyfarthing at a surprisingly high speed. Quickly reacting, Jake jumped out of the way and grabbed the black wool. As the front wheel of the pennyfarthing crossed over, Jake pulled the piece of wool taut, causing it to catch the back wheel, sending the man flying off of his pennyfarthing and into the mausoleum. 
 
 Jake walked into the mausoleum to find that the man had broken through a thin plaster wall and had fallen down the stairs. He followed the stairs down until he reached the dying body of the strange man. Jake bent down to talk to him. 
 
 `` You know, even if you did manage to hit me, you still would have gone flying down here like you did. There's a reason people use cars for hit and runs, and not pennyfarthings.'' 
 
 The man cough more blood out of his mouth and beckoned Jake closer with his finger. Jake brought his ear to the mans mouth. The man died as he said his last words. 
 
 `` You're right. Fucknuggets.'' 
 
 Jake was confused, but banked the word for later usage. He continued walking down the stairs for around three minutes, all the while thinking how much more irritating it would be to have to walk back up. At the bottom of the staircase was a room with a big door on the other end of it. In front of the door were two deep half circles cut into the stone in front of it. Next to the two indents was a refrigerator. A curious Jake opened the refrigerator, and inside found two dozen eggs and a pamphlet. Opening up the pamphlet, Jake found the instructions to get the door open. He had to separate the eggs and fill up both holes, one with egg whites, and the other with the yolks. He started to crack and separate eggs. 
 
 By the time he filled up a third of the yolk hole, the egg white hole was filled. 
 
 `` Damnit,'' he cursed. What am I gon na do with the rest of the egg white?'' 
 
 It was then he heard the sound of two objects sliding, one a stone, and another metal object. He turned to face the refrigerator, and realized that there was a nice electric stove now next to it. On top of the stove was a nice, large pan. Jake turned on the stove to heat up the pan. He then separated the eggs, putting the yolks in the ground and the white in the pan. When he finished, he had an egg white omelet that could keep his family for a week. It was at this moment that Jake remember that he had no family, because his mom was dead. The door slid open, and a couple of stacked, decaying bodies fell from the open door, landing face first in the yolk. Jake walked over the bodies and into the newly opened room, only to find the last set of instructions for Fucknugget Cupcakes. He rolled his eyes and left, wondering why he thought he would find something more than a couple dead bodies and a strange cupcake recipe in the mausoleum, which was, after all, still a mausoleum. 
 
 He wandered back to his mother's grave, only to the find the gravestone lying down on the floor, having been pulled out by the man on the pennyfarthing. Jake sat down and tried to put the gravestone back, but it kept falling back down. Jake grabbed a length of the wool and sat down on a bench nearby, keeping his mother's gravestone slightly angled, but upright. Jake sat still, holding up his mother's gravestone before the police came and arrested him for voluntary manslaughter. The gravestone made a solid sound as it fell back down.
retelling:
Narrative Perspective: The Odd Man/Assailant (Referred to as "Fucknugget" posthumously)

In the grand expanse of an eerie graveyard, I, Fucknugget, found myself drawn towards a particular gravesite - that of Jake's Mother. The pull was inexplicable yet undeniable, my heart racing as I crept closer under the veil of the moonlight. My top hat and monocle, a stark contrast against the darkness, seemed to taunt me with their sinister allure.

I had come prepared for this meeting, armed with an unusual weapon - a rusty trumpet that held a mysterious charm. I knew the graveyard well enough to avoid detection as I made my way towards the gravesite, ready to claim what was mine.

As I reached the grave, my eyes fell upon a piece of black wool attached to it. A curious detail, one that piqued my interest. Intrigued, I followed the thread into the depths of the mausoleum, feeling a strange sense of anticipation wash over me.

Once inside, I was confronted by Jake - a young man whose resolve I underestimated. Our encounter was brief but intense, fueled by the tension that filled the air. I retreated, vowing to return stronger and more prepared for our next meeting.

True to my word, I returned on a penny-farthing bicycle, an ironic choice considering the somber setting. This time, I was determined to claim what I had come for - the black wool that seemed to beckon me from the gravesite.

Our second confrontation was more heated than our first. In a fit of rage and frustration, I lost control, and with one wrong move, I found myself tumbling into the mausoleum's depths. The fall was painful, but it was the sound of my own bones snapping that silenced me forever.

In the aftermath, Jake discovered a hidden room containing a refrigerator with eggs and a pamphlet detailing a puzzle to open a door. He solved the puzzle imperfectly, revealing more decaying bodies and a recipe for "Fucknugget Cupcakes." Ironic, isn't it?

In the end, Jake sat by his mother's grave, the police arriving to arrest him for manslaughter. But little did they know, it was my own recklessness that had led to my demise. The story of our confrontation would live on, a strange tale of mystery and intrigue in the heart of a graveyard.
